item.title: Mount Tsukuba: Twin Peaks & Cable Car Views Over the Kanto Plain — Guide
item.description: Mount Tsukuba, despite standing just 877 m tall, is ranked among Japan’s 100 famous mountains, its distinctive twin peaks (male and female summits) rising dramatically from the flat Kanto plain, visible from a striking distance. A cable car and separate ropeway make the summit accessible without a demanding hike, leading to observation points with panoramic views that, on exceptionally clear days, stretch as far as Tokyo Skytree and Mount Fuji. Hiking trails also wind up the mountain for those preferring to climb on foot.

item.title: Chichibu Plateau & Mount Buko: Hiking Above the Basin — Guide
item.description: The Chichibu Plateau, ringed by mountains including the distinctively quarried Mount Buko, offers some of the most rewarding hiking in the Kanto region within easy reach of Tokyo. Trails of varying difficulty wind across the plateau and its surrounding peaks, opening onto panoramic views over the Chichibu basin below, with cherry blossoms in spring and vivid maple foliage in autumn framing the mountain scenery. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Chichibu, Saitama Hours Trails always open Admission Free Time needed 2–5 hours depending on route Best time Spring (cherry blossoms); autumn (foliage) What to See Panoramic views over the Chichibu basin from plateau trails.
